content: The test image shows soybean plants with lower leaves that are yellowed/brown and wilting/dead, while upper leaves remain green. This pattern of lower leaf necrosis with healthy upper canopy suggests systemic root/stem disease. Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Brown_Stem_Rot, Phytophthora, Septoria_brown_spot.

I've used all 8 reference image views. Let me make my assessment.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows soybean plants with:
- Mostly green, healthy upper canopy
- Lower leaves completely dead, tan/brown, drooping and hanging
- No visible root or stem damage shown

**Comparison to references:**
- **SDS (39, 268)**: Classic interveinal chlorosis with yellow-green veins and brown between — the test lower leaves could be advanced-stage SDS where leaves progressed past interveinal stage to complete death
- **Brown Stem Rot (18)**: Also shows interveinal chlorosis, similar to SDS
- **Phytophthora (2)**: Whole plant wilt/death — doesn't match (upper canopy still green)
- **Septoria brown spot (12)**: Distinct dark spots on yellowing lower leaves — test image lacks visible spotting
- **Fusarium (10)**: Stem symptoms, not leaf death pattern

The most distinguishing feature is the **lower leaf premature death with remaining green upper canopy** — a hallmark of Sudden Death Syndrome. While the classic SDS interveinal pattern isn't visible (leaves are fully dead), the plant-level presentation matches SDS at an advanced foliar stage.
